newsitem.title: MOROCCO: IMF praises Morocco efforts to cut budget deficit.
newsitem.headline: IMF praises Morocco efforts to cut budget deficit.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) praised Morocco's efforts to restructure its economy and reduce its budget deficit, the fund's secretary general Leo Van Houtven was quoted by the official MAP news agency as saying on Tuesday.
"Morocco has registered good economic results this year...The government has recently taken efficient measures to boost the economy and reduce the budget deficit," Houtven said quoted by MAP.
Morocco expects its economy to grow by around 11 percent in 1996.
Houtven, who is on a 48-hour visit, was attending a conference held in Rabat on "World economic globalisation."
He also met Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj and other government officials, MAP said.
Morocco expects its budget deficit to rise to 3.0 percent of Gross Domestic Product in 1996/97, up from the 2.7 percent originally forecast by the government.
Kabbaj said earlier the budget deficit was 5.3 percent in 1995 due mainly to cereal imports after the country was hit by a severe drought.
The state budget envisages 79 billion dirhams receipts for the fiscal year 1996/97. The government changed the fiscal year to run from July 1996 to June 1997, in a referendum last year.
